brief: Goldman Sachs equity sales daily. The S&P closed 58bps lower at 7674, up 12% year to date, with higher oil prices and higher yields named as the standing headwind. The US 10-year sat unchanged at 4.79% and Brent traded close to $100 after Houthi attacks on four Saudi cities and southern oil facilities, with Riyadh promising retaliation, so the oil channel is the note's stated link from the Middle East to the equity tape. Semis outperformed, SOX +1.3% against Mag7 down 19bps, backed by the bank's Tech conference readouts: Broadcom reaffirmed AI revenue growth above 100% for FY27/28, Qualcomm reiterated a $15bn FY29 AI datacenter target and announced a custom-chip partnership with Amazon carrying a warrant over 25 million shares, and hyperscaler capex estimates settled above $1000bn for 2027/28. Retail activity cooled, with Schwab's STAX down from a four-year high on profit taking in high-beta software. NY Fed mean unemployment expectations reached 44.4%, the highest since April 2020. Goldman expects a fully priced 25bps ECB hike tomorrow and thinks September ends the tightening cycle. Copper set a new all-time high above $14500.
